senses.gloss: A large orange-and-black butterfly that migrates south in the fall.
examples: *Monarchs* stop in our yard every September on their way south.
We planted milkweed so the *monarchs* would have somewhere to lay eggs.
A single *monarch* landed on the fence rail.

senses.gloss: A person whose job is to watch over an activity and report on it.
examples: A hall *monitor* stopped us and asked for a pass.
International *monitors* watched the vote count.
The lunchroom *monitor* broke up the argument.

senses.gloss: A device that keeps track of something and warns you about changes.
examples: We keep a baby *monitor* on the dresser.
The heart *monitor* beeped all night.
A carbon monoxide *monitor* hangs in the hallway.

senses.gloss: The feeling that a place, a piece of music, or a work of art creates.
examples: Candles and low music set the *mood* for dinner.
The gray light gives the painting a somber *mood*.
The director uses rain to build a *mood* of dread.

senses.gloss: A natural body that circles a planet other than the earth.
examples: Jupiter has dozens of *moons*.
Titan is the largest *moon* of Saturn.
The probe photographed two small *moons* nobody had seen before.

senses.gloss: A thick, untidy mass of hair on someone's head.
examples: The kid has a *mop* of red curls.
He pushed the *mop* of hair out of his eyes.
A *mop* of blond hair stuck out from under his cap.

senses.gloss: Standards of right and wrong that guide how a person behaves.
examples: He's a man with no *morals* at all.
The scandal raised questions about the mayor's *morals*.
Her *morals* wouldn't let her keep the money.

senses.gloss: A heavy bowl in which spices or medicines are crushed with a pestle.
examples: Grind the garlic and salt together in a *mortar*.
She keeps a marble *mortar* and pestle by the stove.
The old pharmacy sign shows a brass *mortar*.

senses.gloss: A short, heavy gun that fires shells high into the air.
examples: *Mortar* fire hit the edge of the camp.
Soldiers set up a *mortar* behind the wall.
The town came under *mortar* attack at dawn.

senses.gloss: A whole made up of many small, varied parts.
examples: The neighborhood is a *mosaic* of cultures and languages.
From the plane the farmland looked like a *mosaic* of green squares.
His memoir is a *mosaic* of short scenes.

senses.gloss: A formal proposal put to a vote at a meeting.
examples: The *motion* passed by a single vote.
I'd like to make a *motion* to adjourn.
Two members seconded her *motion*.

senses.gloss: A formal request asking a judge to make a ruling.
examples: His lawyer filed a *motion* to dismiss the case.
The judge denied the *motion* for a new trial.
Both sides argued the *motion* on Friday.

senses.gloss: A small hill or a raised pile of earth.
examples: Gophers left *mounds* of dirt all over the yard.
The trail climbs a grassy *mound* above the river.
Archaeologists dug into an ancient burial *mound*.

senses.gloss: A large heap of something piled up.
examples: There's a *mound* of laundry on the bed.
He served us each a *mound* of mashed potatoes.
A *mound* of paperwork was waiting on my desk.

senses.gloss: A horse that someone rides.
examples: She walked her *mount* back to the stable.
Each rider picked a *mount* from the corral.
His *mount* shied at the sound of the shot.

senses.gloss: A soft, airy dessert made with whipped cream and flavoring.
examples: We split a chocolate *mousse* for dessert.
The *mousse* was so light it barely held its shape.
He topped the *mousse* with fresh raspberries.

senses.gloss: The place where a river flows into the sea or a lake.
examples: The port sits at the *mouth* of the Columbia River.
Salmon gather near the river's *mouth* every fall.
Silt builds up at the *mouth* each spring.

senses.gloss: The opening of a cave, a bottle, or another hollow thing.
examples: Bats poured out of the *mouth* of the cave.
Cover the *mouth* of the jar with cheesecloth.
A locked gate blocks the *mouth* of the tunnel.

senses.gloss: The act of changing where you live or work.
examples: The *move* to Denver took us three days.
We hired a company to handle the *move*.
Her *move* to the new office happens in June.

senses.gloss: A movie theater, or a trip there to see a film, usually as 'the movies'.
examples: We took the kids to the *movies* on Saturday.
There's nothing worth seeing at the *movies* this week.
Dinner and the *movies* is our usual Friday.

senses.gloss: An informal word for a person's face.
examples: His *mug* was on the front page of every paper.
Get your ugly *mug* out of my picture.
I'd know that *mug* anywhere.

senses.gloss: A person paid to carry illegal drugs from one country to another.
examples: Customs agents arrested two *mules* at the airport.
The cartel recruits *mules* who need the money.
She was used as a *mule* without knowing what she carried.

senses.gloss: A shoe or slipper with no back, so the heel is open.
examples: She kicked off her *mules* at the door.
Black leather *mules* go with almost anything.
These *mules* slip right on.

senses.gloss: A haircut that is short at the front and sides and left long at the back.
examples: He had a *mullet* all through high school.
The old band photo is nothing but *mullets* and denim.
*Mullets* are apparently back in style.

senses.gloss: Power or influence used to get what you want.
examples: The union has enough *muscle* to stop the deal.
The agency needs more *muscle* to enforce the rules.
Small towns rarely have the political *muscle* to fight back.

senses.gloss: The open front end of a gun barrel.
examples: Smoke curled from the *muzzle* of the rifle.
Never point the *muzzle* at anyone.
*Muzzle* velocity is measured in feet per second.

senses.gloss: A failure to think about anything beyond the immediate future.
examples: The report blames the crisis on corporate *myopia*.
That kind of *myopia* costs a country decades of progress.
There's real *myopia* in planning only for the next quarter.

senses.gloss: A novel, film, or show about solving a crime.
examples: She reads a *mystery* every week.
The library's *mystery* section is by the window.
It's a British *mystery* set in the 1920s.

senses.gloss: The reputation that a person or a business has.
examples: He spent years clearing his *name*.
The company guards its good *name*.
She made a *name* for herself in local politics.

senses.gloss: A well-known person in a particular field.
examples: Several big *names* signed on to the project.
He's the biggest *name* in country music right now.
The conference drew a few famous *names*.

senses.gloss: The basic character or qualities of a person or thing.
examples: It isn't in his *nature* to hold a grudge.
The *nature* of the job changed completely after the merger.
Cats are curious by *nature*.

senses.gloss: The narrow part at the top of a bottle or vase.
examples: He held the bottle by the *neck*.
The cork broke off inside the *neck*.
Foil covers the *neck* of the wine bottle.

senses.gloss: The long thin part of a guitar or violin that carries the strings.
examples: Her hand slid up the *neck* of the guitar.
The *neck* on this bass is too wide for me.
A crack in the *neck* ruined the violin.

senses.gloss: A thick, sweet fruit juice sold as a drink.
examples: I grabbed a can of peach *nectar*.
The recipe calls for apricot *nectar*.
They serve mango *nectar* with breakfast.

senses.gloss: The courage needed to do something frightening.
examples: It takes *nerve* to speak in front of that many people.
He lost his *nerve* halfway up the ladder.
I never worked up the *nerve* to ask her out.

senses.gloss: A state of anxiety, especially before something important.
examples: *Nerves* got the better of him at the audition.
My *nerves* are shot after that drive.
A cup of tea settled her *nerves*.

senses.gloss: A company that broadcasts the same programs on stations across the country.
examples: The *network* canceled the show after one season.
All three *networks* carried the speech live.
She got her start as a *network* correspondent.

senses.gloss: A group of people who stay in contact and help one another, especially at work.
examples: Most jobs come through your *network*.
She built a *network* of clients over ten years.
The alumni *network* is worth joining.

senses.gloss: A system of roads, rails, or lines that cross and connect.
examples: The city's bus *network* runs until midnight.
The storm knocked out part of the power *network*.
A dense *network* of trails covers the park.

senses.gloss: A small bite of food.
examples: She took a *nibble* of the cookie and put it down.
The rabbit took a few *nibbles* of lettuce and hopped away.
One *nibble* was enough to tell me it was burnt.

senses.gloss: A sign that someone might be interested in an offer.
examples: We've had a couple of *nibbles* on the house already.
My resume has been out for a month without a single *nibble*.
The listing got a few *nibbles* but no real offers.

senses.gloss: A small chip or dent in the edge or surface of a thing.
examples: There's a *nick* in the blade of the knife.
The movers left a *nick* in the doorframe.
A few *nicks* in the paint won't hurt the value.

senses.gloss: The rubber tip on a baby's bottle that the baby sucks.
examples: Boil the *nipples* before you use them the first time.
This *nipple* has too slow a flow for him.
She screwed the *nipple* onto the bottle.

senses.gloss: A state of perfect happiness, or the ideal version of something.
examples: For a book lover that store is *nirvana*.
A hot shower after a long hike is pure *nirvana*.
The resort promises three days of *nirvana*.

senses.gloss: Approval, or the choice of one person over others.
examples: She got the *nod* to lead the project.
The rookie got the *nod* to start on Sunday.
The plan still needs a *nod* from the board.

senses.gloss: A small detail that refers to or honors something else.
examples: The remake is full of *nods* to the original.
The menu includes a *nod* to the owner's grandmother.
That line is a clear *nod* to Shakespeare.

senses.gloss: The pointed front end of a plane, a rocket, or a car.
examples: The *nose* of the plane dipped as we came in to land.
Ice built up on the *nose* of the aircraft.
He backed up until the *nose* of the car cleared the curb.

senses.gloss: A natural talent for finding or recognizing something.
examples: She has a *nose* for a good story.
He's got a *nose* for trouble.
A good buyer needs a *nose* for value.

senses.gloss: A step or level on a scale of quality or amount.
examples: Turn the heat down a *notch*.
This year's team is a *notch* above last year's.
Prices went up another *notch*.

senses.gloss: Attention paid to someone or something.
examples: The mistake escaped everyone's *notice*.
Her work finally came to the director's *notice*.
Take no *notice* of what he says.

senses.gloss: A warning given ahead of time that something will happen.
examples: She gave her boss two weeks' *notice*.
The rules can change without *notice*.
They canceled the flight on short *notice*.

senses.gloss: A person who has joined a religious order but has not yet taken final vows.
examples: Three *novices* entered the convent that spring.
As a *novice* he spent his first year almost entirely in silence.
The abbot meets with the *novices* every morning.

senses.gloss: A small piece of valuable information or advice.
examples: The report has a few *nuggets* worth reading.
He gave me a *nugget* of advice I still use.
Buried in the footnotes was a real *nugget*.

senses.gloss: The profession of caring for sick and injured people.
examples: She's going back to school for *nursing*.
Twenty years of *nursing* taught him patience.
The hospital has a serious *nursing* shortage.

senses.gloss: Women's thin stockings, usually called nylons.
examples: She snagged her *nylons* on the corner of the chair.
A pair of *nylons* costs almost nothing now.
Back then no woman went to church without *nylons*.

senses.gloss: In Greek and Roman myths, a young female spirit living in a river, tree, or hill.
examples: The painting shows *nymphs* bathing in a pool.
A *nymph* was said to guard the spring.
In the story a river *nymph* falls in love with a hunter.

senses.gloss: A thing that you can see and touch.
examples: Please take all metal *objects* out of your pockets.
A strange *object* was floating in the pool.
The museum holds thousands of small *objects* from the dig.

senses.gloss: The aim or purpose of an action or a game.
examples: The *object* of the game is to collect all four cards.
The whole *object* of the exercise was to save time.
Winning was never the *object*.

senses.gloss: The person or thing that a feeling or an action is directed at.
examples: He became the *object* of everyone's pity.
She was the *object* of his affection for years.
The mayor is now the *object* of a federal investigation.
